pillar_reactions.evidence: The most engaged reaction to any pillar anywhere in this batch. He volunteered excitement unprompted — 'Well, it's got me excited. I'm fired up to start training this way' — and drove a long stretch of the call with his own questions: how judo builds that kind of strength, how the core is integrated ('I heard Trevor talk about how much it's integrated into all the movements... I'm excited for that just to be a part of my training'), whether doubles are trained early, whether maces are included, and what kettlebell weights to buy. He was sold on the modality before the pillar was delivered and the delivery deepened it.

Never delivered. The rep stopped the pillar sequence after pillar one to screen-share the downsell, and the prospect had to ask for the rest: 'What were the other two pillars? So it's training, mobility, and then...' The entire answer was 'You've got nutrition and then you have the accountability and support pieces.' A named list is not a presentation.

Never delivered beyond the same one-line mention — 'Just obviously, you know, your interaction with Trevor, okay?' — to which the prospect replied 'Gotcha. Cool.' This is the pillar that distinguishes the coaching programme from the $200 course, and it was omitted on the call where that distinction decided the sale.

anchors.raw: I was planning on joining this one today, and then I got a call from Kim, so this started this conversation with the 1-on-1 thing. But I was already ready to go to sign up with this.
anchors.note: The decisive anchor and it was set before the call began. He had already priced the relationship at $200 and had his card out. Every subsequent number would be measured against that, which is exactly why the coaching offer needed to be presented with a reason attached rather than not presented at all.

anchors.raw: Yeah, I actually almost started building a community once in school.
anchors.note: He knows the platform from the operator side and knows what these communities typically cost to run and to join. A prospect who nearly built one himself has an unusually well-calibrated sense of what $200 a month buys.

anchors.raw: I've been an athlete my whole life. I've done various... different types of training from lifting weights, to calisthenics, to resistance bands, to gymnastic rings.
anchors.note: Twenty-eight years old, lifelong athlete, no pain, no injuries, and a track record of teaching himself new modalities. The rep even endorsed it — 'As long as you're disciplined and you seem like you are, then yeah, you should be good' — which is a direct argument against needing coaching, made by the seller.

anchors.raw: it sends a message when someone is fit and capable, and they look solid, it sends a message that they're in control of themselves, and definitely increases people's desire to hear what you have to say, or wanting to work with you
anchors.note: The strongest value anchor available on this call. His physique is a business asset in a coaching practice he is actively building, which makes training a business investment rather than a personal indulgence. Elicited well in Phase 3 and never reused when money came up.

unmet_demand.want: To hear what the one-to-one coaching actually includes — asked for directly: 'I'm open to hearing, too, what the one-on-one looks like'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep did not present it. Coaching was described only in a single comparative sentence ('The coaching program, one-on-one is even more tailored for you') and no price, structure, duration or deliverable was ever given. The prospect made a purchasing decision without the information he had asked for.

unmet_demand.want: Cardiovascular conditioning delivered in a form he will actually enjoy — 'I don't like cardio much and I do a lot of walking for my cardio, but this seems like a more fun way to get my cardio in'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He named this twice as a primary gap. Nobody confirmed whether 30-minute kettlebell sessions three to four times a week deliver the conditioning stimulus he is looking for, or how. The programme very likely does; it was never stated.

unmet_demand.want: An upgrade path from the self-serve product into coaching once he has started
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep gestured at it — 'some people come in here, they enjoy it and then decide, okay, let me see what working with Trevor is like' — but no mechanism, no pricing credit and no follow-up was set. Contrast with the Brady Falks call, where an explicit upgrade credit was quoted. Nothing was booked to revisit this.
